hero_kpi_rationale: Resilient 20.0% operating margin despite volume decline, reflecting operational discipline via the Carlisle Operating System (COS) and structural stability of the renovation market (70% of CCM portfolio).

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin declines in 2025 to 20.0% versus 22.8% in 2024, primarily due to lower fixed cost absorption and increased innovation costs.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total company sales for the year.
kpis.description: Revenue reaches $5.02 billion in 2025, up slightly +0.3% organically, driven by acquisitions in the CWT segment (MTL, PFB, ThermaFoam, Bonded Logic).
kpis.signal: Flat organic growth, driven by acquisitions.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Margin after cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin declines to 35.7% in 2025 versus 37.7% in 2024, due to lower fixed cost absorption over reduced volumes.
kpis.signal: Margin pressure from fixed cost absorption on lower volumes.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development spending as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: R&D spending reaches $47.1 million in 2025, or 0.9% of revenue, up 33.1%, in line with Vision 2030 strategy focused on new product development.
kpis.signal: Marked increase in R&D spending for innovation aligned with Vision 2030.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Gross operating profit adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA stands at $1.225 billion in 2025, down 8% from 2024 ($1.333 billion), primarily due to margin pressure and acquisition integration costs.
kpis.signal: Significant decline due to margin pressure and integration costs.

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.description: The company generates over $1 billion in operating cash flow in 2025, strengthening financial flexibility and share buyback optionality.
kpis.signal: Strong cash generation despite challenging environment.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the past 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $6.26 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the past 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of $2.88 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Re-roofing Market Share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of revenue from renovation rather than new construction.
kpis.description: The re-roofing market represents approximately 70% of CCM segment revenue, a key pillar of Carlisle's resilience against new construction cycles.
kpis.signal: Core business rests on a recurring and resilient market.

kpis.name: Acquisition-Driven Growth
kpis.explanation: Contribution of recent acquisitions to revenue growth.
kpis.description: In 2025, acquisitions (MTL, PFB, ThermaFoam, Bonded Logic) contribute +3.2% to revenue growth, versus -2.9% organic, demonstrating the effectiveness of the M&A strategy.
kpis.signal: Acquisitions offset weakness in organic market.

risks.title: Acquisition Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The company's growth strategy is partially dependent on the acquisition and successful integration of other businesses. Acquisitions involve numerous risks, including failure to realize expected synergies and integration failures.

risks.title: Key Customer Loss
risks.score_rationale: Loss of one or more key customers could negatively impact the business, as certain segments operate in niche markets where a significant portion of revenue comes from a few large customers.

risks.title: Manufacturing Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company could be affected by any significant damage or prolonged disruption to its manufacturing facilities, which could result in uninsured losses and liabilities.

risks.title: New Product Development
risks.score_rationale: Development and introduction of new products are critical to the Vision 2030 strategy, but there are risks related to timing, costs, and commercial success of these new products.

risks.title: Macroeconomic Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to macroeconomic risks, such as interest rate fluctuations, inflation, tariffs, and credit availability, which can affect demand for its products.

ai_positioning.summary: CSL has no significant mentions related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in the provided excerpts from its 10-K/20-F report. Its business appears to focus on areas such as building materials and sealing technologies.
